products.title: Goal!!!
products.body_html:
30 x 40 in

40 x 60 in

 

Goal!!! Together, Jairzinho, Tostão, and Pelé formed one of the most revered attacking units in World Cup history, celebrated for their artistry, movement, and clinical execution. Orlando Abrunhosa’s iconic “Três no Tri” (“Three in the Third”) photograph captures Pelé celebrating with a raised fist, flanked by teammates Tostão and Jairzinho. The image was taken after Pelé scored Brazil’s equalizer against Czechoslovakia in their opening match of the 1970 World Cup in Mexico, helping spark a comeback that ended in a 4–1 win. It is widely regarded as one of the finest sports photographs of the tournament and remains among the most published sports images in the world. 

 

Named FIFA's Player of the Century and the only man to win the World Cup three times, Edson Arantes do Nascimento — known the world over as Pelé — scored 1,283 goals in 1,366 matches. These photographs document his career across four decades, from his earliest years at Santos FC to his legendary performances on the world stage.

 

Hand-signed by Pelé. Each print in this collection carries Pelé's personal signature — making these among the most directly authenticated works of sports photography available to collectors.

 

Printed as a museum-quality Silver Gelatin Print, produced using traditional darkroom techniques on fibre-based photographic paper. Silver gelatin remains the gold standard for black-and-white photography — rich in tonal depth, archivally stable, and built to last generations.

 

Available in strictly limited editions. Each work is supplied with a certificate of authenticity.

products.title: The Bicycle Kick
products.body_html:
30 x 40 in

 

The Bicycle Kick captures one of football's most audacious and beautiful skills — executed by the man who made it famous. This photograph holds the impossible geometry of the moment: Pelé airborne, defying gravity, the ball already on its way to the net. Playing against Belgium in 1968, Pelé is scores whilst his back was towards the goal.

Pelé & Ali brings together two of the twentieth century's defining figures. The greatest footballer and the greatest boxer — photographed together, two giants at ease with their own legend. A meeting of icons that transcends sport. This famous 1977 photograph by Richard Drew captures Pelé embracing Muhammad Ali following Pelé’s final professional soccer match with the New York Cosmos on October 1, 1977.

products.title: Pelé
products.body_html:
40 x 40 in

 

Pelé is a study in presence. Shot at close range, this portrait captures the focus, calm, and gravity of a man who carried the expectations of an entire sport — and delivered on all of them. Photographed by José Dias Herrera, this iconic photograph of a 16-year-old Pelé was taken at Maracanã Stadium (Estádio do Maracanã) in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, during his historic international debut for the Brazilian national team on July 7, 1957. Facing Argentina in the Copa Roca, Pelé came on as a substitute and scored his first international goal, becoming the youngest goalscorer in Brazil’s national team history—a distinction he continues to hold.

products.body_html:

Training Hard, by José Dias Herrera depicts Pelé jumping during a Santos FC training session. Presented in a Santos FC tracksuit, Pelé is captured in a moment that reflects the discipline and athleticism behind his legendary career. José Dias Herrera, is a Brazilian photographer renowned for documenting Pelé and some of football’s defining moments. From the 1950s through the 1970s, Herrera accompanied Pelé as he rose from promising young athlete to global icon.

products.body_html:
30 x 40 in

40 x 60 in

 

This classic 1976 image by Luiz Paulo Machado captures the celebrated moment when sweat on Pelé’s shirt formed a heart across his chest. Widely published and instantly recognizable, the hand-signed photograph held deep personal meaning for Pelé, who called it “a photo only God can explain,” and remains a powerful symbol of his legacy of peace, love, and goodwill.
